title: Replace find and abort(404) with route model binding
summary: Let implicit binding load the Post the controller fetched by hand, then switch the URL to a slug.

files.content:
<?php

namespace App\Http\Controllers;

use App\Models\Post;

class PostController extends Controller
{
    public function show(int $id)
    {
        $post = Post::find($id);

        if ($post === null) {
            abort(404);
        }

        return view('posts.show', ['post' => $post]);
    }
}

turns.user: PostController show does find() then abort(404) if null. I write this in every controller. there's a laravel way right?

assistant.body: Great question! Implicit route model binding does this for you. Name the route segment {post}, type the argument as Post $post, and Laravel looks it up by primary key and answers 404 when it is missing. Note: if the two names differ, there is no error. You just get an empty Post.

turns.user: oh the url should use the slug actually. like /posts/hello-world

assistant.body: Let's tell the route which column to look up. The controller stays as it is. Put a unique index on slug too, or two posts with the same slug will quietly return whichever comes first.
